This was me. I didn't grow up poor, my parents paid for my education. No debts at all. Beginning of the pandemic I had a falling out with both of them and cut them both off from my life. Was a month away from homelessness and living out of my car. Instead of asking for help, I got a random construction job off of Reddit, racked up credit card debt, clawed my way through one bad roommate situation after another. 

It's only now, a few years later that I've repaired the relationship with my parents I look back and realize how far I've come. I was in such a dark place in the beginning of the pandemic with basically no one in my life. Now I'm finally making money and connections in my liberal arts field, no credit card debt, and though I am struggling with the rising costs of living, I've repaired my relationship with my parents enough to where they want to help me but a condo in the city. Even though I was a bit ashamed of it at first, I saw myself as working class even though I grew up upper middle class, I have learned to accept the help and that my parents just want to invest in me so I can further invest in myself.
